intro: Surat has five zones on NXTutors, and the Tapi divides them. The western bank, Adajan, Pal, Palanpur, Rander and Jahangirpura, mixes mid-segment flats and ready societies with Rander's old lanes of family houses. South of the river, the old centre around Nanpura, Athwa and Ghod Dod Road keeps apartments, builder floors and older houses side by side, while Piplod, City Light, Vesu and Dumas Road are newer gated complexes. The southern belt of Udhna, Althan and Pandesara sits beside industrial estates, and north and east of the river, Katargam and Varachha are the diamond side of the city, mostly affordable flats with newer societies further out.

Surat's metro is still being built, so tutors travel by road, rail or bus. Sitilink BRTS corridors run from Adajan Patiya and Pal RTO, along Gaurav Path to Piplod, from Udhana Darwaja to Sachin GIDC Naka, and from Katargam Darwaja towards Kosad and Sarthana. Surat railway station, Udhna Junction, Utran and Kosad add rail links, and autos or two-wheelers finish most trips. The Tapi bridges at office hours, industrial shift changes around Udhna and Pandesara, diamond-unit shifts in Katargam and Varachha, and evening shopping on Ghod Dod Road and VIP Road are the timing points to plan around.

Many Surat students study under GSEB, the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, in Gujarati, English or another medium, so board and medium are matched together, and a Gujarati-medium GSEB student and an IGCSE candidate need different teachers. CBSE, ICSE and ISC are also followed, with the IB and Cambridge IGCSE for a smaller group. Home tuition works well when you stay on your own bank of the river. On the northern edge, in Amroli and Mota Varachha, families can pair a nearby tutor for regular subjects with an online specialist for senior papers, which suits tutors who teach both ways.

zone_notes.Adajan, Pal & Rander: Crossing the Tapi bridges at office hours is the slowest part of any trip here, so tutors who live on the western bank keep slots most easily. Pal and Palanpur societies want your name and the flat at the gate, Rander's old lanes need a landmark and a place for your two-wheeler, and BRTS corridors start at Adajan Patiya and Pal RTO.
zone_notes.Central Surat, Athwa & Ghod Dod Road: Nanpura's narrow lanes suit a tutor on a two-wheeler or in an auto rather than a car hunting for parking. On Ghod Dod Road and around Parle Point, start straight after school, before the evening shopping crowd fills the road, and because the zone sits mid-city, tutors from Adajan, Piplod and City Light can reach it easily.
zone_notes.Piplod, Vesu & Dumas Road: Nearly every home is in a gated society, so ask the family to arrange a standing visitor entry after the demo instead of fresh registration each week. Gaurav Path's BRTS lane brings in tutors who travel by bus, the Red Line is not open to passengers yet, and VIP Road and Dumas Road peak at office hours and weekend evenings.
zone_notes.Udhna, Althan & Pandesara: Housing board blocks and small buildings usually mean going straight to the flat, while Althan and Bhatar societies register you at the gate desk once. Udhna Junction and the Sitilink corridor help, industrial shift changes fill the highway and estate roads, and tutors from Bhatar, City Light or Vesu can reach Althan without crossing the river.
zone_notes.Katargam, Varachha & Sarthana: Diamond-unit shift times shape traffic in Katargam and Varachha, so choose an evening slot that starts after the shift rush. Smaller apartment buildings are a walk-up, newer Mota Varachha and Sarthana societies note visitors on the first day, and Sitilink runs from Katargam Darwaja towards Kosad and along Canal Road to Sarthana.

boards: Surat tutors teach GSEB in Gujarati, English or another medium, as well as CBSE, ICSE and ISC, the IB Diploma and Cambridge IGCSE. GSEB sets the SSC at the end of Standard 10 and separate HSC Science and HSC General exams at the end of Standard 12; its board-published paper designs build each Standard 10 paper with a compulsory section of one-mark objective items. Read paper designs, question banks and results on gseb.org and the board's e-service site, GUJCET notices from the board, CBSE material on cbseacademic.nic.in and CISCE documents on cisce.org.
faqs: How does tuition work reach Surat tutors?

Through matched requests, not open listings. A parent gives the class, board and medium, subjects, area and timings, and NXTutors sends back two or three tutors, closest first: same area, then tutors who travel there, then the zone, Surat and online. The parent sees your fee on the shortlist and books a free demo.
Can Surat tutors take online students too?

Yes. Choose online, home or both. Online requests are matched only on subject, board, class and the hours you are free, so you could teach a GSEB student in Gujarati medium in another district online and still take home classes on your own side of the Tapi.
Should I offer home classes on both banks of the Tapi?

Only if you can cross a bridge on time every week. It is usually easier to keep home classes on your own bank and offer online lessons across the river. If you live south of the Tapi, Piplod, City Light, Vesu, Althan and the old centre are within reach without a bridge.
How does the ID check work for Surat tutors?

When you join, you confirm a phone number or email with a one-time code and upload a government photo ID. Our team reviews it before your profile goes live, and real tutors who pass get a Verified badge. It is an ID check, not a police check; How we verify tutors (/how-we-verify-tutors) explains more.
Do I need to buy a plan to teach in Surat?

Yes, tutor plans are paid, and the Pricing page (/pricing) sets out what each plan covers. You set your own lesson fee, which Surat families see on your profile before the free demo. Parents can change tutor without paying more, so arriving on time through the shift-change rush keeps a family with you.
